raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

When more LoRA adapters are busy than there are slots, the scheduler skips waiting requests whose adapter doesn't fit. As long as the adapters in the batch keep receiving requests, they keep their slots, and every other adapter waits until one of them happens to go idle. With 4 busy adapters on 3 slots (benchmark below), 1% of requests on `main` wait about **90 seconds** for their first token, compared to a median of **77 ms**.

#### Example

Consider 3 slots held by adapters A, B and C, which all receive steady traffic, while adapter D waits. Whenever A, B or C finishes a request, another request for it is already queued, so D never gets a slot. With this PR, once D has waited longer than `--lora-drain-wait-threshold`, the drainer drains B, the adapter that will leave the batch soonest. B stops admitting requests that would outlast the ones it is running, leaves the batch when they finish, and D takes its slot.

```
main
  slot 0 │███ A ██████████████████████████████████│
  slot 1 │███ B ██████████████████████████████████│
  slot 2 │███ C ██████████████████████████████████│
  D      │░░░ waiting ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│

this PR
  slot 0 │███ A ██████████████████████████████████│
  slot 1 │███ B ██████████▒▒ B drains ▒▒███ D ████│
  slot 2 │███ C ██████████████████████████████████│
  D      │░░░ waiting ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░          │

█ running   ▒ admits only requests that finish with its running ones   ░ waiting
```

## Modifications

I rewrote `LoRADrainer` (`python/sglang/srt/lora/lora_drainer.py`), which `--lora-drain-wait-threshold` turns on. Note that this feature is off by default:

* An adapter is starving once its oldest waiting request has waited longer than the threshold. When the batch is full, the drainer drains one running adapter per starving adapter, longest wait first.
* A drain ends once the drained adapter leaves the batch, or once the starving adapter gets a slot or has nothing waiting.

## Accuracy Tests

* Revamped the unit tests in `test_lora_drainer.py`
* All LoRA tests pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling

I benchmarked on a single H200 with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (MoE) and four adapters. To benchmark `main` and my branch:

1. Start the server (for `main`, drop `--lora-drain-wait-threshold 3`):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 \
    --enable-lora \
    --max-loaded-loras 4 \
    --max-loras-per-batch 3 \
    --lora-drain-wait-threshold 3 \
    --lora-paths \
        adapter0=mindlab-research/Macaron-A2UI-Tall \
        adapter1=hsilvosa/hsc-wuxia-qwen-3-30b-a3b \
        adapter2=tarsur385/tau2_bench_synthetic-grpo-iter50 \
        adapter3=manjunathshiva/opendecider-medium-td
```

2. Run a benchmark where more adapters are busy than there are slots:

```
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --dataset-name random \
    --num-prompts 800 \
    --request-rate 4 \
    --random-input-len 512 \
    --random-output-len 512 \
    --lora-request-distribution uniform \
    --lora-name \
        adapter0 \
        adapter1 \
        adapter2 \
        adapter3
```

#### Results

| Metric | `main` | PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Benchmark duration (s) | 218.9 | 218.6 | −0.1% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 907.2 | 908.3 | +0.1% |
| Mean E2E latency (ms) | 17,124 | 9,605 | **−43.9%** |
| Median E2E latency (ms) | 7,526 | 8,880 | +18.0% |
| P99 E2E latency (ms) | 95,087 | 25,539 | **−73.1%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 26.14 | 26.15 | +0.0% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 24.20 | 26.03 | +7.6% |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 42.39 | 36.89 | **−13.0%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 10,820 | 3,172 | **−70.7%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 77 | 149 | +92.6% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 89,612 | 14,350 | **−84.0%** |

On `main`, the adapter left without a slot waits until another one happens to go idle, so the slowest requests wait well over a minute. With the drainer, slots rotate once a request has waited 3 s, which bounds every adapter's wait at the same throughput. Median TTFT and E2E rise because the requests `main` leaves waiting are now served alongside the others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -31,7 +31,7 @@ The following server arguments are relevant for multi-LoRA serving:
 
 * `max_lora_chunk_size`: Maximum chunk size for the ChunkedSGMV LoRA backend. Only used when --lora-backend is 'csgmv'. Choosing a larger value might improve performance. Please tune this value based on your hardware and workload as needed. Defaults to 16.
 
-* `lora_drain_wait_threshold`: When any LoRA adapter request waits longer than this threshold (in seconds), the scheduler will selectively drain one running adapter to make room. This mitigates extreme tail latency under high or skewed workloads by preventing a small set of adapters from monopolizing batch slots. Set to 0 to disable draining (default).
+* `lora_drain_wait_threshold`: Once an adapter's oldest waiting request exceeds this threshold (seconds), the scheduler can drain an unpinned running adapter to make room. Multiple adapters can be drained when several waiting adapters need slots. Each drain limits new requests to a fixed running request's remaining output budget. Pinned adapters are never drained. This is best effort: the threshold starts draining without reserving a freed slot or guaranteeing a maximum waiting time. Set to 0 to disable draining (default).
 
 * `tp_size`: LoRA serving along with Tensor Parallelism is supported by SGLang. `tp_size` controls the number of GPUs for tensor parallelism. More details on the tensor sharding strategy can be found in [S-Lora](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.03285) paper.

+"""CPU-only tests for LoRA draining and adapter-slot admission."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Optional, cast
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.lora.lora_drainer import LoRADrainer
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+NOW = 1000.0
+LORA_DRAIN_WAIT_THRESHOLD = 3.0
+STARVING_WAIT = LORA_DRAIN_WAIT_THRESHOLD + 1.0
+
+
+def make_req(
+    lora_id: Optional[str],
+    max_new_tokens: int = 10,
+    waited_secs: float = 0.0,
+    finished: bool = False,
+) -> Req:
+    """A stand-in for `Req` with only the fields the drainer reads."""
+    req = SimpleNamespace(
+        lora_id=lora_id,
+        time_stats=SimpleNamespace(wait_queue_entry_time=NOW - waited_secs),
+        sampling_params=SimpleNamespace(max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens),
+        output_ids=[],
+        finished=lambda: finished,
+        is_retracted=False,
+    )
+    return cast(Req, req)
+
+
+def starving_req(lora_id: Optional[str]) -> Req:
+    return make_req(lora_id, waited_secs=STARVING_WAIT)
+
+
+class TestLoRADrainer(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        patcher = mock.patch("time.monotonic", return_value=NOW)
+        patcher.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
+
+    def make_drainer(self, max_loras_per_batch: int) -> LoRADrainer:
+        return LoRADrainer(max_loras_per_batch, LORA_DRAIN_WAIT_THRESHOLD)
+
+    def assert_draining(self, drainer: LoRADrainer, lora_id: str):
+        # Running requests in these tests need at most 100 tokens.
+        self.assertFalse(drainer.can_schedule(make_req(lora_id, max_new_tokens=1000)))
+
+    def assert_not_draining(self, drainer: LoRADrainer, lora_id: str):
+        self.assertTrue(drainer.can_schedule(make_req(lora_id, max_new_tokens=1000)))
+
+    def test_longest_waiting_adapter_drains_the_adapter_closest_to_done(self):
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=2)
+        waiting = [make_req("A", waited_secs=STARVING_WAIT + 1), starving_req("D")]
+        running = [make_req("B", max_new_tokens=5), make_req("C", max_new_tokens=100)]
+        drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, running)
+
+        # 'A' has waited longest, and 'B' will leave the batch first.
+        self.assertEqual(drainer.drained_adapter_to_drain["B"].starving_adapter, "A")
+        self.assertEqual(drainer.drained_adapter_to_drain["C"].starving_adapter, "D")
+
+    def test_drain_ends_when_the_drained_adapter_leaves_the_batch(self):
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=1)
+        waiting = [starving_req("A")]
+        drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, [make_req("B")])
+        self.assert_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+        drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, [])
+        self.assert_not_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+    def test_drained_adapter_only_admits_requests_that_finish_with_it(self):
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=1)
+        running = [make_req("B", max_new_tokens=100)]
+        drainer.update_draining_state([starving_req("A")], running)
+
+        # 'B' has 100 tokens left.
+        self.assertTrue(drainer.can_schedule(make_req("B", max_new_tokens=100)))
+        self.assertFalse(drainer.can_schedule(make_req("B", max_new_tokens=101)))
+
+    def test_drained_adapter_admits_nothing_once_its_anchor_stops(self):
+        for reason in ("finished", "retracted"):
+            with self.subTest(reason=reason):
+                drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=1)
+                waiting = [starving_req("A")]
+                anchor = make_req("B", max_new_tokens=100)
+                admitted = make_req("B", max_new_tokens=50)
+                drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, [anchor, admitted])
+
+                anchor.finished = lambda: reason == "finished"
+                anchor.is_retracted = reason == "retracted"
+                # Preemption can retract the anchor during the same admission pass.
+                self.assertFalse(drainer.can_schedule(make_req("B", max_new_tokens=1)))
+
+                # A shorter request keeps B running after the anchor leaves.
+                if anchor.is_retracted:
+                    waiting.append(anchor)
+                drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, [admitted])
+                self.assertFalse(drainer.can_schedule(make_req("B", max_new_tokens=1)))
+
+    def test_drain_ends_once_the_starving_adapter_no_longer_needs_a_slot(self):
+        """A drain whose starving adapter needs no slot must stop rejecting requests."""
+        running_b = make_req("B", max_new_tokens=5)
+        running_c = make_req("C", max_new_tokens=100)
+        name_to_case = {
+            # 'C' left the batch on its own and 'A' took its slot.
+            "starving adapter got a slot": (
+                [starving_req("A")],
+                [make_req("A"), running_b],
+            ),
+            # 'A' has nothing waiting anymore, e.g. its requests were aborted.
+            "starving adapter has nothing waiting": ([], [running_b, running_c]),
+        }
+        for name, (waiting, running) in name_to_case.items():
+            with self.subTest(name):
+                drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=2)
+                drainer.update_draining_state(
+                    [starving_req("A")], [running_b, running_c]
+                )
+                self.assert_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+                drainer.update_draining_state(waiting, running)
+                self.assert_not_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+    def test_adapter_in_the_batch_does_not_drain_others(self):
+        """An adapter in the batch must not drain others for its own waiting requests."""
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=2)
+        # If 'A' could drain others, it would drain 'B': 'B' has fewer tokens left.
+        running = [make_req("A", max_new_tokens=100), make_req("B")]
+        drainer.update_draining_state([starving_req("A")], running)
+        self.assert_not_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+    def test_base_model_can_trigger_a_drain(self):
+        """Starving base-model requests (lora_id None) must trigger a drain too."""
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=1)
+        drainer.update_draining_state([starving_req(None)], [make_req("B")])
+        self.assert_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+    def test_pinned_slots_only_drain_an_adapter_that_can_make_room(self):
+        """Idle pins still occupy slots; finishing a pin cannot free its slot."""
+        for pin_running in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(pin_running=pin_running):
+                drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=2)
+                running = [make_req("A", max_new_tokens=100)]
+                if pin_running:
+                    running.append(make_req("P", max_new_tokens=5))
+                drainer.update_draining_state(
+                    [starving_req("B")], running, pinned_loras={"P"}
+                )
+                self.assert_draining(drainer, "A")
+                self.assert_not_draining(drainer, "P")
+
+    def test_finished_requests_do_not_hold_a_slot(self):
+        """A finished request still in the batch must not keep its adapter's slot."""
+        drainer = self.make_drainer(max_loras_per_batch=2)
+        # If 'C' still held a slot, 'B' would be drained: it has fewer tokens left.
+        running = [make_req("B"), make_req("C", max_new_tokens=100, finished=True)]
+        drainer.update_draining_state([starving_req("A")], running)
+        self.assert_not_draining(drainer, "B")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
